annotations.text:
A — Academic Green

Deep forest green with a gold accent; Newsreader for headings over Public Sans.

Keeps today's density and card anatomy exactly — only palette and type change, so it is the cheapest to ship and the least risky.

Tradeoff: reads traditional and collegiate. Safe, but it will not turn heads.

B — Civic Navy

Institutional navy with a teal accent; IBM Plex throughout. Tighter rows, 6px radii, more rows per screen.

Built for volume work — a bursar reconciling fees or a head scanning eleven classes sees more without scrolling.

Tradeoff: the most efficient and the least warm. Parents meet it only on the report card, where it reads governmental.

C — Warm Paper

Cream ground, clay primary, olive accent; Instrument Serif over Karla. Larger radii, more air.

The most distinctive, and by far the best printed report card — it looks like a document a school is proud to hand over.

Tradeoff: lowest information density, and a cream ground is harder to read on a cheap phone in bright sun — worth weighing for Ghana.
